title: Nonvanishing of I for n>=2: thm:newvector asserted, not proved (the one live gap)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Context (current `solution.tex` = "A Universal Test Vector").** The revised draft correctly reduces the whole theorem (via `lem:unfold` + `cor:sindep`) to the single $s$-independent constant
$$I \;=\; \int_{K_n}\psi(-Q\,k_{nn})\,V(k)\,dk ,\qquad V=\text{normalized newvector of }\pi .$$
The collapse to a single $\det$-shell, the uniformity of the $\pi$-independent $W_0$, and the $n=1$ Gauss-sum nonvanishing ($|I|^2=q^{-c}$, verified numerically) are all **complete and correct**. The remaining content is entirely:

$$\boxed{\;I\neq 0\ \text{ for every generic }\pi,\ \text{conductor }c\ge 1,\ n\ge 2.\;}$$

**The gap.** `thm:newvector` (eq. `matringe`) asserts this but does NOT prove it. The "Why this holds" paragraph is heuristic and has two unjustified steps:

1. It claims that "choosing the conductor-matching test function $\Phi_Q$ supported near $Q^{-1}e_n$ converts the right-hand zeta integral $Z(s,V,\Phi)=\int_{N_n\backslash G_n}V(g)\Phi(e_n g)|\det g|^s\,dg$ into the Gauss sum $I$." This conversion is **never carried out**, and is non-obvious: $I$ weights only the single entry $k_{nn}$ and integrates over the full compact $K_n$, whereas $Z(s,V,\Phi)$ depends on the **entire last row** $e_n g=(g_{n1},\dots,g_{nn})$ via $\Phi$. Identifying $I$ with a value/residue of $Z(s,V,\Phi_Q)$ requires an explicit unfolding that is missing.

2. It then says the result "is the content of Matringe's essential-vector computation [Matringe, Thm 1.1, §3]." Matringe computes $Z(s,V,\mathbf 1_{\mathfrak o^n})=L(s,\pi)$ and essential-vector Whittaker values; he does **not** directly state $\int_{K_n}\psi(-Q\,k_{nn})V(k)\,dk\neq 0$. The citation is a pointer to a tool, not a proof.

**What must be proved.** For every generic irreducible admissible $\pi$ on $\mathrm{GL}_n$, $n\ge2$, conductor $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p^c$ with $c\ge1$, and the normalized newvector $V$:
$$\int_{K_n}\psi(-Q\,k_{nn})\,V(k)\,dk \neq 0 .$$
(The $c=0$ sub-case is trivial: $\psi(-Qk_{nn})=1$ and $V$ spherical give $I=V(1)=1$.) One must also confirm that the **newvector** is a valid choice of $V$ here — a priori a twisted average of $V|_{K_n}$ could vanish; the problem only requires *some* $V$.

**Suggested route.** Mirror the $n=1$ Gauss-sum proof at level $n$: use the Iwasawa/mirabolic decomposition of $K_n$, push $V$ down via its left-$(N_n,\psi)$-equivariance and $K_1(\mathfrak q)$-invariance, and reduce the $\psi(-Qk_{nn})$-twisted integral to a primitive additive Gauss sum of $\mathfrak o/\mathfrak q$ in the $(n,n)$-coordinate (nonzero by conductor matching $|Q|=q^c$). Alternatively, express $I$ via the JPSS local functional equation $\gamma(s,\pi,\psi)$ and units, forcing a unit. Either way, exhibit the transfer steps explicitly.

This is the single remaining mathematical obstacle to a complete proof in the current draft.
